Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demo last week. As part of our procurement checklist I need to confirm a few items about your Dedicated deployment model for our tenant:

- Can you confirm that a tenant pinned to a US region (us-west-2) will never have runtime data (KV cache, ephemeral disk, backups) replicated outside that region?
- What controls ensure tenant-by-tenant segregation at the hypervisor or container level?
- For compliance we need an auditable proof that data was deleted when we request an erasure (chain-of-custody, timestamps, and hashes). Can you provide a sample certificate or an example output that Redwood would generate post-wipe?

I've attached our security questionnaire for your reference (commerce_security_qs.pdf). Our legal/infosec team needs a timeline for evidence delivery if we raise an erasure request during a contract window.

Appreciate a short write-up or a time to jump on a call.

Thanks,

Emma — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Priyom (platform) and Marissa (CS) so we can produce a concise package. High level answers below; Priyom will follow with the technical runbook and example evidence.

- Region pinning: tenants can be pinned to a single region at the control-plane level. Requests are routed with regional affinity and storage volumes are created in the pinned region by default.
- Isolation: we use tenant-scoped namespaces + stricter VM affinity for Dedicated pools; compute instances are labeled and scheduled with tenant isolation constraints. Network egress for tenant volumes is restricted to the VPC/subnet in that region.
- Deletion evidence: we can generate a certificate containing timestamps, resource IDs, and sha256 hashes of wiped files (where applicable) plus an operator sign-off.

Next steps: Priyom will attach the internal runbook excerpt and a sample erase certificate. Marissa — please confirm lead times for scheduling a maintenance window if CommerceTech requests a forced purge.

Best,

Emma — thanks, here are the concrete operational controls and the evidence artifacts we produce. Longish but I wanted to be explicit so your infosec has everything to evaluate: 

1) Region pinning & replication controls- Instance placement: Dedicated tenant workloads are scheduled on GPU/CPU pools whose nodes are tagged with region IDs; scheduling policy enforces strict node affinity (no cross-region scheduling).
- Storage: Block volumes and object storage snapshots for tenant projects are provisioned in-region. Cross-region replication is disabled by default for Dedicated (can be enabled only with explicit customer opt-in and a documented request).
- Backups: Automated backups are stored in-region; cross-region archival requires explicit config and is off for CommerceTech per current dev notes.

2) Segmentation layers- Network: Tenant VPC peering and security groups limit egress; we also use host-based firewall rules on compute nodes.- Compute: Tenant namespaces isolate containers; for hard isolation we place tenants into separate VM groups on pinned hosts.

3) Deletion / Erasure process (what we log and deliver)- Trigger: Customer-initiated erasure request via Console or support ticket.
- Action: We iterate through resources (KV caches, ephemeral disks, attached block volumes, backups) and execute a wipe sequence: secure zeroization for ephemeral disks, crypto-key destruction for encrypted snapshots, and object deletion for storage buckets.
- Evidence: After wipe we generate an erase certificate (CSV + signed metadata) that includes: resource_id, resource_type, wipe_method, operator_id, start_timestamp, completion_timestamp, sha256_digest_of_previous_manifest (where applicable), and a short chain-of-custody note.

4) Example audit snippets (redacted)
- resource: tenant-ct-54321/kv-cache-epoch-182
  wipe_method: zeroize-in-place
  start: 2028-05-12T02:15:03Z
  complete: 2028-05-12T02:15:09Z
  operator: ops-erasure-03
  manifest_hash: 3a7b2f4e...

5) Chain-of-custody & verification- We keep an append-only event log (immutable) that records the API calls that triggered wipe events. We can provide hashes of that log and a signed certificate from the operator. For higher assurance customers we can also provide a notarized PDF with operator signature.

6) Timing and SLA- Typical evidence package availability: 36-72 hours after the erasure window completes (depends on queued work and legal hold checks). If you need a tighter SLA we can negotiate as part of the Dedicated contract (reserved capacity customers often add a 24/48 hour evidence SLA).

Attachment: region_wipe_playbook_v1.pdf (internal runbook excerpt)

I will prepare a sample erase_certificate_20280512.csv once we run a test purge in our staging tenant and share it externally.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
